name: LT1122 (fast-settling JFET-input single op-amp, grades A/B/C/D)
tagline: Linear Technology's 14 MHz, 80 V/us fast-settling JFET single; a niche rollers' pick for DAC output/filter stages, named alongside the LT1361, LT1364 and LT1469.
technology: Single-channel, voltage-feedback, internally compensated (unity-gain stable) op-amp with JFET inputs. Per the ADI/LTC datasheet (1122fb): 80 V/us slew, 340 ns settling, 14 MHz bandwidth at 7 mA supply current, 120 uV offset, voltage gain 500,000, aimed at fast-settling 12-bit data conversion and acquisition. LTC's SPICE macromodel uses a P-channel JFET input pair with a 2.25 mA tail current.

reputation.summary: A niche, cult-level pick with no mainstream following. Head-Fi op-amp rollers name the LT1122 as a candidate alongside the LT1361, LT1364 and LT1469 in a thread on DAC output stages. diyAudio members group it with the LT1028 and LT1115 as Linear Technology chips worth trying and call the LT1122ACN8 'a good chip' (second-hand, unverified wording). Tangent's op-amp listening notes (Chinese translation on Soomal, 2005) list it among chips to test later, with no verdict. No Audio Science Review or Samuel Groner measurements are known. Outside audio, a KiCad reproduction of the HP 3458A A3 board uses an LT1122 as unity-gain buffer U404.
sonic_descriptors: 'a good chip' (diyAudio, general praise; no specific sonic descriptors verified)
typical_uses: DAC output and reconstruction-filter stages (Head-Fi recommendations)
Single op-amp rolling in DIP-8 sockets (LT1122ACN8 / CCN8)
Fast-settling buffers for 12-bit data conversion and acquisition (datasheet design intent)
Precision instrument buffers: HP 3458A A3 board U404 (KiCad reproduction)
caveats: Single channel only: dual-op-amp sockets need an adapter carrying two of them.
About 7 mA quiescent current per amplifier (datasheet), so it runs warmer and drains batteries faster than TL07x-class parts.
Fast part (14 MHz, 80 V/us): treat like other fast op-amps (good decoupling, short leads); stability in a given socket not verified.
Grades A-D probably differ in DC or settling guarantees (not verified); for audio the grade is unlikely to matter.
Voltage-noise density and THD were not confirmed; the datasheet markets speed and settling, not low noise, so do not assume it is a low-noise audio part.

datasheets.title: The LT1122 Fast Settling JFET Op Amp, by George Erdi et al. (Linear Technology Magazine)
datasheets.note: This is the LTC introduction article, not a datasheet. It describes the original design: a modified bipolar-FET (poly-gate JFET) process, 14MHz GBW, 80V/us, and 340ns settling to 1mV for a 10V step. It is supporting evidence for the original silicon, and its issue date would give the introduction date.

counterfeit_notes: No LT1122 counterfeit or remarking reports are known (not specifically searched in this pass). Low-volume, single-source LTC/ADI part. Buy from authorized distributors; be wary of cheap marketplace 'LT1122ACN8' lots; check the LTC logo, grade letter (A/B/C/D) and date-code plausibility; confirm about 7 mA quiescent current at +/-15 V and roughly 14 MHz / 80 V/us behaviour. A re-marked slow JFET part such as a TL071 would draw far less current and be far slower.

revision_chain_notes: Linear Technology / Analog Devices LT1122 (sole source; no second source found). Known chain, oldest to newest: [original LTC edition, date unknown, probably c. 1989-1990: MISSING, no copy with a shown date or print code found] -> [Rev A: MISSING. It is not logged in the Rev B revision-history table, and no copy showing 'Rev A' or an older LT print code turned up in 4 searches] -> Rev B, 1122fb, 02/14 (LT 0214 REV B), 'updated to current standards'. ADI still hosts Rev B unchanged as the current edition. Newly found candidate copies that may hold pre-2014 editions, none with the revision shown: DatasheetQ -Linear-V2 (the second of two versions), the datasheetarchive.com LT1122 and LT1122CC indexes (the ceramic CC suffix points to an early edition), datasheetbank, aipcba, and datasheet4u (probably the same file as datasheetspdf 1078518). The Linear Technology Magazine introduction article by George Erdi (Scribd copy) documents the original design but has no issue date in the search summary. Next step: check Wayback snapshots of http://www.linear.com/product/LT1122 and http://cds.linear.com/docs/Datasheet/lt1122.pdf. They should show the pre-2014 edition and its print code (e.g. 'LT/xx yy'). The alldatasheet 70317 upload is probably the oldest scan to compare against 1122fb.
